Decades ago, most of the large-scale assembly lines for LPTs were offshored, and their reestablishment in the United States necessitates a skilled workforce and significant financial investment. To understand the current LPT assembly landscape, we conducted interviews with suppliers and people in the industry. They emphasized that demand will keep growing because of electrification and the growth of data centers. Manufacturers are focusing on making new high- capacity units (100–200 MVA and above, some classified as 230 kV and others as >345 kV). Experts pointed out that there will be $2 billion in new investments in U.S. manufacturing, but imports are still needed for units over 345 kV and 765 kV. One U.S. GOES manufacturer makes a small amount of high-quality or premium GOES and is working to improve its capabilities. They shared that Nippon Steel’s purchase of U.S. Steel has stabilized the short-term steel outlook. But tariffs still make it hard to import goods from targeted countries, which limits sourcing options. Suppliers do not consider components such as tanks and housings as problems but say that bottlenecks in specialized parts are the biggest problem. People who were interviewed said that bushings and OLTCs are now the biggest risks in the market. COVID made existing problems worse. Before the pandemic, it took from 40 weeks to a year to get 230-kV bushing. Now, 345-kV bushings take more than 130 weeks, and there are no domestic suppliers for 765-kV bushings. There are only two U.S. manufacturers that support the 345-kV market and none that cover the 765-kV market. Global companies are still limited in capacity, and customer wait times increase if specific types of insulators are ordered (e.g., resin- 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. impregnated synthetic, resin-impregnated paper, and oil-impregnated synthetic) that require additional lead time. As a result, the only option is to rely on available inventory. U.S. manufacturers also import bushings and OLTCs from Germany and Switzerland. The current lead time to manufacture bushings and OLTCs is about 80 to 90 weeks, even though companies are working to increase their capabilities. Some regional suppliers of CTC have exited the market, which has forced remaining companies to take additional orders. The United States has a few producers of pressboard and insulating materials, but there are not many options outside of China. Stakeholders said that winding is still a long and difficult process, even though final assembly is fairly quick. They also said that it is difficult to find and train qualified workers. The interview process revealed that even though long-term demand is clear and domestic investment needs more time to bear fruit, the U.S. LPT supply chain is still structurally weak because of long lead times, limited infrastructure, and a lack of skilled workers in the domestic market. 1.6 Estimated Regional Pricing Regional pricing for LPTs in the United States varies significantly due to transportation logistics, labor market conditions, and project-specific needs.
